verdict: test-only issues corrected; ready for separately authorized real Docker qualification after the campaign

correctedFindings.finding: Original early-Fatal cleanup cancelled Run but immediately reconciled and deleted TempDirs without joining its worker. This could race an active worker/lease or erase ownership records.
correctedFindings.correction: Dedicated completion signal; cleanup cancels and closes the owned proxy, waits for Run, and reconciles journals only after join. A bounded emergency path removes only owner-checked test guests if join times out, waits again, and skips journal recovery if still active. Manually owned state/workspace directories are retained and logged on unjoined worker or failed recovery; they are removed only following successful reconciliation.

correctedFindings.finding: The upstream-to-client EOF path closed both sockets, potentially discarding final client-to-upstream bytes even though the peer only half-closed its output.
correctedFindings.correction: Both copy directions now CloseWrite their destination and wait for the other direction; explicit proxy close still closes all active sockets and joins its workers. Local Unix fixtures exercise client-first and server-first half-close ordering plus eight concurrent closes while streams are active.

correctedFindings.finding: Parent readiness originally raced the first detached-child heartbeat, and a merely existing heartbeat could be stale when recovery began.
correctedFindings.correction: Guest waits for the child heartbeat before signalling ready; test then requires heartbeat advancement after socket loss and before recovery, followed by stable heartbeat after guest removal.

correctedFindings.finding: Post-loss CLI/reconciliation/fresh-run assertions relied only on the overall test context.
correctedFindings.correction: A separate one-minute deadline bounds the qualification recovery phase; cleanup uses fresh bounded contexts.

reviewedProperties: Proxy drops only its temporary Unix listener and accepted sockets; it does not stop or reconfigure Docker Desktop or affect other clients.

Proxy listener and forwarding workers participate in a WaitGroup; admission/close tracking is serialized with the mutex, close is idempotent through sync.Once, and active socket closure unblocks both copy loops.

The fresh executor uses the real configured Docker socket and unique test state owner label. Recovery admission, unpublished source preservation/discard, owned container removal, child heartbeat stop and fresh read-only command assertions remain present.
Test-owned filesystem state is retained for explicit recovery rather than silently removed if the bounded cleanup cannot establish completion.

validation.command: env -u GEMMA_TEST_DOCKER_IMAGE GOPATH="$PWD/.cache/go" GOCACHE="$PWD/.cache/gobuild" GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.10 go test -race -json ./internal/execution -run '^TestDocker(SocketProxy.*|LiveConnectionLossDiscardsAndRecoversOwnedGuest)$' -count=5
validation.qualification: Only local Unix listeners were enabled. The real Docker test compiled and skipped five times because GEMMA_TEST_DOCKER_IMAGE was explicitly unset.

remainingLimits: No actual Docker attach, connectivity-loss recovery, detached-child termination or source-discard result is claimed by this review. The real opt-in test remains pending until after campaign completion.

The test simulates a client transport loss through an owned proxy. It does not qualify a Docker daemon/VM crash, host power loss, or actual application restart; the fresh executor object qualifies durable ownership recovery within the same test process.

If Docker itself is unavailable during cleanup or the worker cannot be joined after bounded emergency removal, the test fails and retains/logs its private recovery paths for explicit maintenance. It cannot guarantee remote guest termination while the daemon is unreachable.
